## `loadout`

```text
Manage MCP servers, skills and secret references for AI coding clients

Usage: loadout [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  doctor         Check the installation and report problems
  server         Manage MCP servers in the store
  skills         Skills: install, enable for clients and projects, update, scan
  agent          The read-only Loadout skill for coding agents: install, remove, status, skill-path
  source         Trusted and blocked install sources: list, trust, block, untrust
  catalog        Catalogs of MCP servers and skills: list, add, search, show
  scanner        Scanners: the built-in scanner and the optional Snyk Agent Scan (install, turn on or off, token reference, run)
  project        Project manifests: create, register, trust, share, list, forget
  history        List store commits
  status         Show the state of every owned and desired entry
  diff           Show the apply plan as file diffs
  effective      Show what each client loads in a folder, and from where
  apply          Reconcile client files with the store (one commit per run)
  rollback       Roll back an apply run
  show           Show one store commit and what it changed
  tag            Create, list or delete store tags
  restore        Restore the store (or client files) from an earlier state
  backup         Commit hand edits of the store and optionally tag the result
  remote         Backup and sync remotes (none by default)
  import         Import foreign client entries into the store
  adopt          Take ownership of foreign or changed client entries
  migrate        Migrate from SkillDock (~/.skilldock is only read)
  secrets        Secret references: aliases, providers and their status
  env            Print export statements for secret aliases
  secret         Print one resolved value (internal, for client command hooks)
  secret-header  Print resolved headers as JSON (internal, for Claude Code `headersHelper`)
  exec           Start an MCP server with secrets from its references (launch delivery); never writes to stdout
  help           Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --home <PATH>  Data directory to use instead of LOADOUT_HOME or the per-OS default
      --json         Print machine-readable JSON to stdout
      --yes          Answer yes to confirmations (rolling back an older apply run)
  -h, --help         Print help
  -V, --version      Print version
```

## `loadout doctor`

```text
Check the installation and report problems

Usage: loadout doctor [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --home <PATH>   Data directory to use instead of LOADOUT_HOME or the per-OS default
      --paths         Also report the resolved OS folders and data directory layout
      --json          Print machine-readable JSON to stdout
      --scan-history  Also scan every store commit for secrets (reports only; history is never rewritten)
      --yes           Answer yes to confirmations (rolling back an older apply run)
  -h, --help          Print help
```

## `loadout server`

```text
Manage MCP servers in the store

Usage: loadout server [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  ls        List servers
  show      Print a server definition
  add       Add a server, or (--from) draft servers from a git repository or a local folder
  rm        Remove servers; several ids make one commit
  update    Update servers added with --from (all, or ID) to what their source gives now; --check only reports
  checkout  Re-create or bring up to date this machine's checkout of a server added with --from that runs from its repository (`LOADOUT_HOME/servers/<ID>`), at the commit its file names. The same gates as `add --from`: source trust, then the scan
  help      Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --home <PATH>  Data directory to use instead of LOADOUT_HOME or the per-OS default
      --json         Print machine-readable JSON to stdout
      --yes          Answer yes to confirmations (rolling back an older apply run)
  -h, --help         Print help
```

## `loadout server add`

```text
Add a server, or (--from) draft servers from a git repository or a local folder

Usage: loadout server add [OPTIONS] [ID] [-- <COMMAND>...]

Arguments:
  [ID]
          Server id: 1 to 64 characters from a-z, 0-9, '.', '_', '-'. With --from: the id of the one draft saved [default: from its name]

  [COMMAND]...
          Command and arguments of a stdio server, after `--`

Options:
      --home <PATH>
          Data directory to use instead of LOADOUT_HOME or the per-OS default

      --url <URL>
          Endpoint of an http or sse server

      --json
          Print machine-readable JSON to stdout

      --transport <TRANSPORT>
          Transport [default: stdio, or http with --url]
          
          [possible values: stdio, http, sse]

      --env <KEY=VALUE>
          Environment variable of a stdio server; the value may be a reference such as ${secret:ALIAS} and is never a secret itself

      --yes
          Answer yes to confirmations (rolling back an older apply run)

      --header <NAME=VALUE>
          HTTP header of an http or sse server; the value may hold references

      --cwd <CWD>
          Working directory of a stdio server

      --display-name <DISPLAY_NAME>
          

      --description <DESCRIPTION>
          

      --tag <TAG>
          Tag (repeatable)

      --client <CLIENT>
          Enable at system scope for this client (repeatable)

      --all-detected
          Enable at system scope for every detected client

      --from <GIT-URL|PATH|catalog:SOURCE/ID>
          Draft servers from a git repository (https, ssh, file://, a bare repository) or a local folder: server.json, an MCPB manifest.json, committed client configs, or the repository as a package. Or from a catalog entry: catalog:<SOURCE>/<ID> (`loadout catalog search`)

      --path <PATH>
          Folder inside the git repository

      --ref <REF>
          Branch, tag or commit of the git repository; for a registry catalog entry, the version (pins it: updates do not follow)

      --pick <KEY|ID>
          The draft to save, by key or id (repeatable) [default: the only draft]

      --all
          Save every draft

      --dry-run
          List the drafts, their inputs and scan findings; save nothing (the clone is removed)

      --trust-source [<ONCE|REPO|OWNER|HOST>]
          Answer the source trust prompt up front: once (this save only), or always for the repo, its owner or its host. Only for a source you trust: a server drafted from it runs its commands. --yes never answers the trust prompt

          Possible values:
          - once:  Install or update this time only
          - repo:  Always trust this repository
          - owner: Always trust every repository of this owner
          - host:  Always trust every repository on this host (not for public hosts such as github.com)

      --allow-dangerous
          Save even when the built-in scan finds dangerous content (review the findings first, with --dry-run)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `loadout skills`

```text
Skills: install, enable for clients and projects, update, scan

Usage: loadout skills [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  ls       List store skills (and the agents CLI's skills when compatibility is on)
  add      Install a skill from a git URL, a local folder, or a .zip/.skill archive. With --yes, a taken id becomes <id>-2. A git source you have not trusted asks first (a terminal prompt, or --trust-source). The built-in scan runs first; a dangerous verdict installs nothing (exit 8) unless --allow-dangerous
  rm       Remove a store skill and its owned links and copies; with --agents, remove an agents CLI skill through the `skills` CLI
  enable   Enable a skill for clients (user scope), or in a project
  disable  Disable a skill for clients (user scope), or in a project
  update   Update git skills (all, or ID); --check only reports. A source you have not trusted (or whose trust lapsed after a force-push or a move) asks first. Each new content is scanned first; a dangerous one is not applied (exit 8) unless --allow-dangerous
  scan     Classify the client skill folders: managed, unmanaged, mismatch
  import   Import an unmanaged folder of a client's skill folder into the store
  trash    Move an unmanaged or mismatched entry of a client's skill folder to the trash (backups/trash), never deleting it
  vendor   Copy an agents CLI skill (~/.agents/skills) into the store
  adopt    Adopt unmanaged folders of client skill folders (SPEC 8.6, 12.5): import them into the store, enabled where they were found, and replace each folder whose content equals the store copy with a link (the folder moves to backups/trash). Folders with the same content in several clients become one skill. Without NAME, --all, --pick or --both, lists what can be adopted
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --home <PATH>  Data directory to use instead of LOADOUT_HOME or the per-OS default
      --json         Print machine-readable JSON to stdout
      --yes          Answer yes to confirmations (rolling back an older apply run)
  -h, --help         Print help
```

## `loadout skills add`

```text
Install a skill from a git URL, a local folder, or a .zip/.skill archive. With --yes, a taken id becomes <id>-2. A git source you have not trusted asks first (a terminal prompt, or --trust-source). The built-in scan runs first; a dangerous verdict installs nothing (exit 8) unless --allow-dangerous

Usage: loadout skills add [OPTIONS] <SOURCE>

Arguments:
  <SOURCE>
          Git URL (a GitHub /tree/<ref>/<path> URL selects a folder), a local folder or archive, a catalog entry (catalog:<SOURCE>/<ID>), or a skills.sh address (https://skills.sh/<owner>/<repo>/<skill>)

Options:
      --home <PATH>
          Data directory to use instead of LOADOUT_HOME or the per-OS default

      --path <PATH>
          Skill folder inside a git repository

      --json
          Print machine-readable JSON to stdout

      --ref <REF>
          Branch, tag or commit of a git repository (a commit pins the skill)

      --id <ID>
          Skill id [default: from the SKILL.md name]

      --yes
          Answer yes to confirmations (rolling back an older apply run)

      --allow-dangerous
          Install even when the built-in scan finds dangerous content (review the findings first)

      --external
          Also run Snyk Agent Scan on it this time (sends the skill to Snyk), even when it is turned off

      --no-external
          Do not run Snyk Agent Scan this time, even when it is turned on

      --trust-source[=<ONCE|REPO|OWNER|HOST>]
          Trust the git source without the prompt: once (this install only), or always for the repo, its owner or its host (`--trust-source=repo`; the value needs the `=`). Only for a source you trust: skills can run commands and read your files. --yes never answers the trust prompt

          Possible values:
          - once:  Install or update this time only
          - repo:  Always trust this repository
          - owner: Always trust every repository of this owner
          - host:  Always trust every repository on this host (not for public hosts such as github.com)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `loadout skills enable`

```text
Enable a skill for clients (user scope), or in a project

Usage: loadout skills enable [OPTIONS] <ID>

Arguments:
  <ID>  

Options:
      --client <CLIENT>  Client id (repeatable) [enable default: all detected clients; disable default: every client]
      --home <PATH>      Data directory to use instead of LOADOUT_HOME or the per-OS default
      --json             Print machine-readable JSON to stdout
      --project <PATH>   A project folder: edit its manifest's [skills] enable instead
      --copy             Distribute as copies
      --yes              Answer yes to confirmations (rolling back an older apply run)
      --link             Distribute as links (the default)
      --symlink          On Windows, make directory symbolic links instead of junctions (needs Developer Mode or admin rights)
  -h, --help             Print help
```

## `loadout skills update`

```text
Update git skills (all, or ID); --check only reports. A source you have not trusted (or whose trust lapsed after a force-push or a move) asks first. Each new content is scanned first; a dangerous one is not applied (exit 8) unless --allow-dangerous

Usage: loadout skills update [OPTIONS] [ID]

Arguments:
  [ID]
          

Options:
      --check
          Report available updates; update no skill. A trusted source found force-pushed or moved still has its trust lapse (one store commit), so the next install or update from it asks

      --home <PATH>
          Data directory to use instead of LOADOUT_HOME or the per-OS default

      --agents
          ID names an agents CLI skill, updated through the `skills` CLI

      --json
          Print machine-readable JSON to stdout

      --allow-dangerous
          Apply updates even when the built-in scan finds dangerous content (review the findings first, with --check)

      --yes
          Answer yes to confirmations (rolling back an older apply run)

      --external
          Also run Snyk Agent Scan on each available update this time (sends the new content to Snyk), even when it is turned off

      --no-external
          Do not run Snyk Agent Scan this time, even when it is turned on

      --trust-source[=<ONCE|REPO|OWNER|HOST>]
          Trust the git sources without the prompt: once (this update only), or always for the repo, its owner or its host (`--trust-source=repo`; the value needs the `=`, so `--trust-source repo` updates the skill `repo` once)

          Possible values:
          - once:  Install or update this time only
          - repo:  Always trust this repository
          - owner: Always trust every repository of this owner
          - host:  Always trust every repository on this host (not for public hosts such as github.com)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `loadout skills adopt`

```text
Adopt unmanaged folders of client skill folders (SPEC 8.6, 12.5): import them into the store, enabled where they were found, and replace each folder whose content equals the store copy with a link (the folder moves to backups/trash). Folders with the same content in several clients become one skill. Without NAME, --all, --pick or --both, lists what can be adopted

Usage: loadout skills adopt [OPTIONS] [NAMES]...

Arguments:
  [NAMES]...  Folder names to adopt (each with one content)

Options:
      --all                 Adopt every name that has one content
      --home <PATH>         Data directory to use instead of LOADOUT_HOME or the per-OS default
      --json                Print machine-readable JSON to stdout
      --tool <CLIENT>       Only this client's skill folder [default: every client]
      --project <PATH>      The skill folders of this project (trusted) instead of the user folders; adopted skills go to its manifest's [skills] enable
      --yes                 Answer yes to confirmations (rolling back an older apply run)
      --pick <NAME=CLIENT>  For a name with several contents: adopt the content in CLIENT's folder (or `store`, the store's copy) as NAME; folders with other content are kept (repeatable)
      --both <NAME=CLIENT>  Adopt CLIENT's content (or `store`) as NAME and every other content as NAME-<client> (repeatable)
  -h, --help                Print help
```

## `loadout scanner`

```text
Scanners: the built-in scanner and the optional Snyk Agent Scan (install, turn on or off, token reference, run)

Usage: loadout scanner [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  ls       List the scanners: the built-in scanner (always on) and Snyk Agent Scan (optional)
  status   Show Snyk Agent Scan on this machine: version, installed, on or off, the token reference, and what it sends to Snyk
  install  Download the pinned Snyk Agent Scan build into the data directory and verify its SHA-256. Installing does not turn it on
  remove   Delete the installed scanner and turn it off (the token reference is kept)
  enable   Run Snyk Agent Scan on skill installs and updates. It sends each skill to Snyk's analysis API: see `loadout scanner status`
  disable  Stop running Snyk Agent Scan; nothing is sent to Snyk
  token    Show, set or clear the token reference: a secret alias (see `loadout secrets`) or env:NAME, keyring://SERVICE/ACCOUNT or op://VAULT/ITEM/FIELD. Never the token itself
  run      Scan a library skill (its store content) with Snyk Agent Scan now; reports only. Sends the skill to Snyk
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --home <PATH>  Data directory to use instead of LOADOUT_HOME or the per-OS default
      --json         Print machine-readable JSON to stdout
      --yes          Answer yes to confirmations (rolling back an older apply run)
  -h, --help         Print help
```

```text
      --files <APPLY-ID>          Restore client files from the backups of this apply run instead
      --yes                       Answer yes to confirmations (rolling back an older apply run)
      --file <PATH>               With --files: only this client file
      --from <DIR|ZIP|BARE-REPO>  Restore from a folder remote, machine folder, bare repository, mirror or zip
      --machine <ID|LABEL>        With --from: the machine to restore from, by id or label
  -h, --help                      Print help
```

## `loadout import`

```text
Import foreign client entries into the store

Usage: loadout import [OPTIONS] [NAME]...

Arguments:
  [NAME]...  Entry names to import; all importable entries when none

Options:
      --home <PATH>
          Data directory to use instead of LOADOUT_HOME or the per-OS default
      --scan
          List candidates, their sources, conflicts and secrets; change nothing
      --client <CLIENT>
          Only entries of this client (repeatable)
      --json
          Print machine-readable JSON to stdout
      --scope <SCOPE>
          Which files to read: user files (system), the files of the known projects, or both [default: all] [possible values: system, project, all]
      --yes
          Answer yes to confirmations (rolling back an older apply run)
      --project <ID>
          Only the files of this known project (its id)
      --only
          Copy the definitions without enabling them (no ownership taken)
      --pick <NAME=CLIENT>
          Import NAME as CLIENT has it, under NAME (repeatable; picks one definition of an entry that differs between clients). CLIENT may be a source key from --scan (omp#work, claude-code@PROJECT-ID) for a client's other file
      --as <NAME=CLIENT>
          Import NAME as CLIENT has it, as NAME-CLIENT (repeatable; with --pick, imports both definitions). CLIENT may be a source key
      --skip <NAME>
          Leave NAME out (repeatable)
      --extract <NAME[:FIELD]=DEST>
          Where NAME's literal secrets go: keyring, op://VAULT/ITEM/FIELD, op-env://ENV/NAME or env:VAR. NAME:FIELD (env.KEY, headers.KEY, args[N], url) sets one field (repeatable)
      --remove-old-backups[=<APPLY-ID>]
          Remove the client file backups that still hold the old values of extracted secrets: those of this import's apply, or with =APPLY-ID those of an earlier import (then nothing is imported). Undoing that import can then no longer bring those files' earlier content back
  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `loadout secrets`

```text
Secret references: aliases, providers and their status

Usage: loadout secrets [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  ls               List aliases with this machine's reference and the servers using them
  check            The missing-secret checklist: resolve aliases and report their status (never their values), the servers and clients that need them and how to fix them; exits 5 when one cannot be resolved. May prompt for 1Password approval
  providers        Show which secret providers this machine has
  set              Set an alias's reference
  clear            Delete the OS keyring entry of an alias's keyring reference on this machine; the reference stays
  map-op-env       Map the variables of a 1Password Environment to aliases (`op-env://<ENV-ID>/<NAME>`) and save the Environment id
  op-account       The 1Password account Loadout's `op` calls use, for machines whose desktop app is signed in to several accounts: show it, set it, or clear it
  service-account  The 1Password service account token in the OS keyring, passed by `loadout exec` to `op` only
  help             Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --home <PATH>  Data directory to use instead of LOADOUT_HOME or the per-OS default
      --json         Print machine-readable JSON to stdout
      --yes          Answer yes to confirmations (rolling back an older apply run)
  -h, --help         Print help
```
